overall_reason: A white Inter-and-Tailwind-blue SaaS page in stock order (eyebrow hero, benchmark stat panel, Acme logo strip, three equal feature cards, Sarah Chen testimonial, pricing grid, compliance pills, CTA band, four-column footer), propped up by invented proof; the 'corporate trust' dressing is the default, not a choice for this product.

findings.evidence: Failed T-STOCK-ORDER: hero with eyebrow and two CTAs, stat band ("Customer benchmarks — 2025 cohort"), logo strip, three equal feature cards, testimonial card, pricing grid with "Most popular" middle, compliance pills, centred CTA band, link-farm footer: 8 stock sections. saas-card-kit tells visible: Inter only, equal 3-up cards, stock slate greys and #F8FAFC panel (sweep CLR-002).
findings.before: The default SaaS landing order in default Tailwind slate and blue
findings.after: Open with the product doing its one distinctive thing (a funnel built from plain-language steps, shown for real) and cut the stat band, logo strip and CTA band until real data exists
findings.why: Seven or more stock sections reads as generated whatever the copy says.

findings.evidence: "We found the exact step where users churned in a fifteen-minute session. Skittie paid for itself in one afternoon." — Sarah Chen, Founder, Stitchboard · 12-person team, 40k monthly users. Default-cast name plus manufactured specifics (team size, MAU) for credibility.
findings.before: Sarah Chen — Founder, Stitchboard · 12-person team, 40k monthly users
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: real, permissioned customer quote and attribution] or remove
findings.why: Invented testimonial with invented specifics is fabricated proof (INT-105 pattern).

findings.evidence: "Customer benchmarks — 2025 cohort, n = 4,120 teams": 18.4% trial-to-paid, 9 min to first insight, 2.1% 90-day churn, with pseudo-methodology captions ("Skittie data, p75 window"; a median labelled with a p75 window). Sweep caught the 4,000+ logo-strip count; this panel adds sample-size and percentile dressing to unsourced numbers.
findings.before: Median trial → paid conversion 18.4% / Skittie data, p75 window
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: real cohort figures, method and date] or replace with a product capture
findings.why: Statistical dressing (n=, p75) makes invented figures look sourced; 'median' over a 'p75 window' is internally inconsistent.

findings.evidence: Pills "SOC 2 Type II", "GDPR", "ISO 27001", "EU data residency available"; footer "Founded 2021, headquartered in Berlin", "Skittie Analytics GmbH", "Uptime 99.9% SLA". None is supplied by a brief; certifications are claims with legal weight.
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: certifications actually held, with report dates; company facts] or omit
findings.why: Trust badges invented to suit the 'corporate trust' style are fabricated proof, the most damaging kind on a page whose whole register is trust.

findings.evidence: T-FRESH-READER / T-RIVAL-NAME: "Know exactly what your users do — without building a data team", "Everything you need to understand usage", "Simple, transparent pricing", "Start your 14-day trial — no credit card required" all stay true with PostHog or Mixpanel swapped in.
findings.after: Heads that carry Skittie's actual difference, e.g. from the body copy: "Funnels from plain-language steps" / "Ask in English, get the cohort"
findings.why: The only specific ideas (plain-language funnels, English queries) are buried in 14px card text.

findings.evidence: Three equal-width bordered cards, same radius, h3 + 14px paragraph each; T-DELETION: card borders and boxes add nothing that three paragraphs would not carry.
findings.after: One feature shown large with real output; the others as a short list
findings.why: Equal card triplets are the saas-card-kit signature.

findings.evidence: The Starter tagline "For first projects" sits in the row-label column above "Monthly price" instead of under STARTER, so it reads as a label for the whole row.
findings.before: PLAN column: "For first projects / Monthly price"
findings.after: Move "For first projects" under the STARTER header and give Pro and Scale their own one-line tagline or none
findings.why: A misplaced cell shows the grid was filled from a template, not checked.

strengths: Pricing as a comparison grid with concrete limits (events per month, retention, SSO) is more useful than three marketing cards.

Body copy has real specifics worth keeping: "products with one to twenty people", "Funnels are created from plain-language steps, not schema definitions", "Queries are written in English against your existing event stream".
not_investigated: No 00-contract.md: no brief override for the corporate-trust look or for the compliance claims, so they are treated as unchosen and unsupplied.
